title: Atmospheric extras bundle — scene fog + ACES filmic tonemap + persistent vignette (Three.js built-ins)
intent: Per `docs/game-design/threejs-references-analysis.md §2.1 + §2.8 + §2.9`. Three small Three.js built-ins bundled as one story — each negligible cost, combined impact is 'the game suddenly looks polished'. (1) Scene fog — per-theme atmospheric tint that fades far cells into the theme colour. (2) ACES Filmic tonemap — replaces default linear tonemap so emissive accents (cyan pickups, red bomb-pulse, lit theme accents) don't clip to white. (3) Subtle persistent vignette — gentle darkening at screen edges that reinforces the diorama framing. Combined: scenes get a 'professionally graded' look without any geometry / shader / asset changes.
rationale: Source: `docs/game-design/threejs-references-analysis.md §5.2` (recommended bundle). All three effects are built into Three.js or trivially expressed (renderer flags + simple shaders). Combined visual quality lift is high relative to ~50 LOC + ~1ms / frame cost. Bundling them as ONE story avoids 3 separate small stories all touching the same render init path.
acceptanceHints: DEPENDS ON: GDP-2026-05-28-013 (per-arena themes — fog colour is per-theme).
Builds on top of GDP-2026-05-28-001 (lighting/shadow primitive — adds tonemapping to the renderer setup).
PART 1 — SCENE FOG (per-theme):
Three.js' `Scene.fog = new FogExp2(color, density)` adds exponential distance-tinted fog. No new render passes, integrates natively.
Theme schema extension (extends ArenaTheme from GDP-013):

fogColor: '#hex' — theme-specific colour. Defaults per theme: warehouse #707068 (warm grey haze), factory #4a3a28 (smoky red-brown), dock #707890 (cool sea mist), lab #c8d0d6 (clean haze), bunker #2e2c28 (dim drab).
fogDensity: number (0..0.05) — default 0.012. Lower = subtler.
ArenaThemeApplySystem (from GDP-013): on theme apply, set Scene.fog = new FogExp2(theme.fogColor, theme.fogDensity).
Disable / opt-out: `?fog=off` URL flag clears scene.fog. Screenshots + bot-vs-bot tests may want this.
PART 2 — ACES FILMIC TONEMAPPING:
Three.js' renderer setting: `renderer.toneMapping = THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping`. One line change in renderer init.
Also: `renderer.toneMappingExposure = 1.0` (default), tunable for global brightness.
Per-theme `tonemapExposure: number` (0.7..1.3, default 1.0) — themes can adjust overall exposure. Lab theme could be brighter (1.15), bunker theme could be dimmer (0.85).
ApplySystem reads theme + sets renderer.toneMappingExposure on theme apply.
Disable: `?tonemap=linear` URL flag forces linear (current behaviour).
PART 3 — PERSISTENT VIGNETTE:
Postprocessing pass — small fragment shader that fades pixel alpha (or multiplies colour by a circular falloff) at screen edges.
Visual style: ~10% darkening at the very screen edges, fading to 0% at ~40% of screen radius from centre. Subtle — should NOT be obvious as a 'filter'.
Implementation: either via Three.js EffectComposer + ShaderPass, OR via a custom screen-quad rendering pass after the main scene. ShaderPass is simpler; preferred.
Vignette colour: matches the current theme's ambient ground colour (theme.ambientHemisphericGround from GDP-013). Pulls the framing INTO the diorama colour family.
Disable: `?vignette=off` URL flag.
INTEGRATION POINTS:
examples/kaboom-crew/bootstrap.ts: render-init step gets ACES tonemap + EffectComposer with vignette pass enabled.
ArenaThemeApplySystem extended with the three apply paths (fog setting, tonemap exposure, vignette colour).
No new generic engine module — these are Three.js built-ins applied at project bootstrap. Pure project-side wiring.
PERFORMANCE:
Fog: ZERO cost (vertex/fragment built-ins).
Tonemap: ZERO cost (renderer setting).
Vignette: ~0.3ms / frame (full-screen pass with simple shader).
Combined ~0.3ms / frame. Within budget.
MULTIPLAYER: pure presentation. Per-tab. No protocol changes.
DETERMINISM: visual only. Gameplay-state-deterministic per gameplay-systems.md §12.1.
INTERACTIONS:
Bloom (existing): tonemap goes AFTER bloom in the pipeline. Bloom contributes emissive glow; tonemap renders it nicely without clipping.
Outline-occluder (GDP-2026-05-28-014): the outline pass runs BEFORE vignette so outlined bombers are clearly visible.
Camera follow + closer framing (S163): vignette stays anchored to screen edges — doesn't move with camera. Subtle framing reinforcement.
UNIT TESTS:
Scene.fog set after theme apply.
fogColor matches theme value.
renderer.toneMapping = ACESFilmicToneMapping after init.
renderer.toneMappingExposure matches theme's tonemapExposure.
Vignette ShaderPass added to EffectComposer.
URL flags individually disable each effect.
VISUAL QA:
Load warehouse theme arena → grey fog softens distant cells. Emissive accents (cyan pickups) glow softly without clipping. Subtle edge darkening.
Switch to lab theme → fog whiter, exposure brighter, scene feels clean.
Switch to bunker theme → fog dimmer + darker, exposure lower, scene feels gloomy.
Compare to default-render (without tonemap + fog + vignette): default looks 'flat'; with bundle, scene looks 'graded'.
DOCS UPDATES IN THIS PR:
visual-style.md §4.2 — mark fog, ACES tonemap, vignette as 'shipped' in the Post-FX table. Reset their status from 'allowed' to 'shipped'.
Theme table in GDP-013 stories — note the fogColor + tonemapExposure fields added per theme.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Bloom (already shipped before — reaffirm it lives in the pipeline correctly with tonemap).
SSAO (separate Post-FX pipeline story; not in this bundle).
SMAA / FXAA (separate; not in this bundle).
Camera shake (visual-style.md §6.3 explicit ban remains).
Animated fog density (changes during sudden-death). Static per theme.
Dynamic vignette (intensifies during low-health). Visual-style.md §4.2 already lists low-health vignette as a separate feature — this bundle is the BASELINE static vignette.
Procedural skybox (Three.js webgl_shaders_sky.html). Separate possible follow-up; not in this bundle.
